assessment-2-3-vision-simulation-and-ora.title: Assessment 2.3 – Vision simulation and oral demonstration
assessment-2-3-vision-simulation-and-ora.summary: Locate five coloured shapes and four calibration markers, estimate pixel-to-robot XY and demonstrate five valid simulator moves with your own oral explanation.
assessment-2-3-vision-simulation-and-ora.body:
> [!abstract] TL;DR
> Use a warped RGB image to locate five coloured shapes and four red calibration markers, calculate a homography from image pixels to the robot's XY plane and move all five shapes with [CoppeliaSim](/egb339/temaer/coppeliasim). Upload the code before the deadline and explain your solution individually in your registered week-13 practical. Source: *task sheet pp. 1–4*.

## Requirements and marking

- The five movable objects are **red square**, **blue circle**, **blue square**, **green circle** and **green square**. You may choose their starting and target positions in simulation, but every object must move at least **75 mm**. The tolerance is **5 mm**. *Task sheet p. 2*.
- You may choose the parameters of the initial image warp. Demonstrate and explain object localisation, colour/shape, marker ordering, homography, image→robot XY and robot motion. *Task sheet pp. 1–2*.
- The functional demonstration is worth 2.5 percentage points and oral conceptual understanding 10 percentage points. Missing either the code upload or demonstration gives 0/12.5; the PDF export shows **18 October 2026**, but check the current Canvas deadline and time before submission. *Task sheet p. 1*, *pp. 3–4*.
- The oral component lasts **5–15 minutes** and requires your own explanation of algorithms, results, limitations and tests. Example questions concern area/perimeter, salt-and-pepper noise, blob counting and colour classification under varying illumination. *Task sheet pp. 3–4*.

## Calibration and robot geometry

| Parameter | Simulation |
| --- | ---: |
| $L_0,L_1,L_2,L_3,L_4$ | 138, 135, 147, 60, **80** mm |
| Four red markers, clockwise from the large one | $(178,22.5)$, $(223,22.5)$, $(223,-22.5)$, $(178,-22.5)$ mm |
| Maximum final object-position error | 5 mm |

The markers are not the five movable objects. The ordering in *both* the image and XY lists must agree; the largest red circle is the first point. *Task sheet p. 2*, [Calibration markers and image warping](/egb339/temaer/calibration-markers-and-image-warping).

## Supplied files and interface

`assignment_2_3_vision.zip` contains `PickAndPlacerobot.py`, `testPickAndPlace.py`, `coppeliaRobot.py`, `genericRobotAPI.py`, `prac_2.ttt`, `reference_values.pkl` and the Pixi manifest/lockfile. The template defines **`PickAndPlaceRobot(robotObj, img, target_positions)`**, plus `PickUp`, `Place` and `ikine`. Preserve the filename and required function interface. `testPickAndPlace.py` contains five example targets and a scene test harness. An old comment mentions `wordTypingRobot.py`; it is inconsistent with this task sheet and template. *Supplied ZIP*, *task sheet p. 2*.

The template intentionally contains placeholders: `pick_position` and `place_position` are both `[183,0,177]` in the loop, and `ikine` raises `NotImplementedError`. This is **not** a finished solution. *Supplied ZIP*.

## Algorithm chain and reference functions

RGB image → colour masks → [mask cleaning](/egb339/temaer/binary-morphology) → [blobs and centroids](/egb339/temaer/connected-components-and-image-moments) → [shape](/egb339/temaer/shape-descriptors-from-area-and-perimeter) → four correctly ordered markers → [pixel-to-XY H](/egb339/temaer/planar-homographies) → [IK](/egb339/temaer/inverse-kinematics) → safe pick-and-place.

Optional `REF_` functions cover shape localisation, marker ordering, homography, image→XY and IK. The task warns of deductions and cumulative dependencies when they are used; make this choice consciously against the rubric. Reference values describe only the original scene configuration, not a general calibration. *Task sheet pp. 1–2*.

## Study plan and related notes

- [Assessment 2.3 and 2.4 – Pick-and-place implementation plan](/egb339/ressurser/assessment-2-3-and-2-4-pick-and-place-implementation-plan) — build the solution yourself, test each stage and port only after validating the simulation.
- [Week 9 – Feature extraction and spatial operators](/egb339/uker/uke-9), [Week 10 – Colour](/egb339/uker/uke-10) and [Week 11 – Image formation and image geometry](/egb339/uker/uke-11) supply the principal vision tools.
- [Assessment 2.4 – Vision physical robot submission](/egb339/vurderinger/assessment-2-4-vision-physical-robot-submission) uses the same idea, but **different** marker coordinates, $L_4$ and safety rules.

> [!tip] Your own checks, not additional assignment requirements
> Inspect detected objects, centroids, marker order, homography reprojection and final robot errors separately. This isolates a fault before moving the robot. The task sheet does not supply universal colour thresholds; check them against the images.

## Open questions

- Which thresholds and shape descriptors remain stable under changes to the initial warp or lighting?
- How is marker order validated when a red object resembles a calibration circle?
- How is the 5 mm error measured independently of the homography used for control?

assessment-2-4-vision-physical-robot-sub.title: Assessment 2.4 – Vision physical robot submission
assessment-2-4-vision-physical-robot-sub.summary: Port vision-guided pick-and-place to physical Dobot with different calibration and geometry. Move only the four requested objects among eight, within absolute safety/time limits.
assessment-2-4-vision-physical-robot-sub.body:
> [!abstract] TL;DR
> Port the validated image→XY→pick-and-place chain from [Assessment 2.3 – Vision simulation and oral demonstration](/egb339/vurderinger/assessment-2-3-vision-simulation-and-oral-demonstration) to the physical Dobot. The function receives one prewarped input and a dictionary of four targets; eight shapes are visible. Safety and time limits are absolute. Submit only `PickAndPlacerobot.py`. *Task sheet pp. 1–4*.

## Interface and data

Gradescope calls **`PickAndPlaceRobot(robotObj, img, target_positions)`**. Arguments are the physical robot API, *one* randomly warped `mvt.Image` and a dictionary of desired XY positions. All eight objects are visible: green triangle/square/circle, blue triangle/square/circle and red square/triangle. **Four** requested objects must move; iterate the relevant `target_positions` keys, not all eight automatically. *Task sheet p. 1*, *p. 4*.

Submit only `PickAndPlacerobot.py`. Remove imports/references to `coppeliaRobot`; the supplied `PickUp` annotation can use `robotObj` without the simulator class. Do not acquire a new image or read joint/end-effector status on the physical robot. *Task sheet p. 4*.

## Physical constants — do not reuse 2.3 values

| Parameter | Physical 2.4 |
| --- | ---: |
| $L_0,L_1,L_2,L_3,L_4$ | 138, 135, 147, 60, **70** mm |
| Four red calibration markers, clockwise from the large one | $(117.7,154.8)$, $(297.7,154.8)$, $(297.7,-165.2)$, $(117.7,-165.2)$ mm |
| Object height | 9 mm |
| Accepted target error | within 20 mm |
| Recommended contact tip height | $z=8$ mm |

The markers are planar references, not movable objects. The $L_4$ and marker values are **different** from 2.3. *Task sheet p. 3*.

Starting positions and targets are random within the workspace. Object centres and targets should normally be at least **50 mm** apart, but these are guidelines, not an absolute guarantee; markers may be up to **10 %** partially occluded. Make classification/marker detection robust and do not rely on one particular scene. *Task sheet p. 3*.

## Abort limits and timing

> [!warning] An aborted job counts as an attempt
> - Never command the suction tip below $z=6.5$ mm.
> - After picking/releasing, lift to **at least $z=31$ mm** before any lateral movement. Later on p. 3 the recommendation is $z=30$ mm; use the stricter $31$ rule from the abort list, preferably with an extra margin.
> - The entire function must finish within **3 minutes**.
> - Do not call `get_joint_config()`, `get_end_effector_pose()` or `get_image()`.
> - Do not use blocking displays such as `plt.show()` or `img.disp(block=True)`.
>
> Source: *task sheet pp. 2–3*.

Physical `move_arm(j1,j2,j3)` blocks, so the simulator's `time.sleep()` is unnecessary. For logging during a long job, use `robotObj.print(str(...))`, which writes the server log; ordinary `print()` output may be absent. *Task sheet pp. 3–4*.

## Score and attempts

The task gives $\max(0,2.5C-P-\min(7,\max(1.75N-5.25,0)))$, where $C$ is correctly placed objects out of four, $P$ is the reference-function deduction and $N$ is submission count. The first three attempts have no attempt penalty; beyond seven attempts the maximum possible score is 3/10. The PDF export shows **21 October 2026**, and the text says Wednesday 4 pm; check the current Canvas time/time zone before submission. *Task sheet p. 1*, *p. 5*.

## Example images and checks

`VisionExampleImages-2024.zip` contains **ten pairs** (`0`–`9`) of `*_original.png` and `*_warped.png`; `__MACOSX` metadata files are not images. Originals are for debugging only: calculate calibration from warped images resembling the actual input. The images show four red markers and eight coloured objects, not the simulator's five-object set. *Image archive*, *task sheet p. 4*.

> [!tip] Your own porting strategy
> Make colour/shape, ordering, homography and pixel→XY testable without the robot. Then change the 2.3 constants and motion policy in a configured 2.4 variant. Check all ten warped images and test the safety sequence with a fake robot before spending a physical submission attempt.

## Further study

- [Assessment 2.3 and 2.4 – Pick-and-place implementation plan](/egb339/ressurser/assessment-2-3-and-2-4-pick-and-place-implementation-plan) gives the combined workflow.
- [Calibration markers and image warping](/egb339/temaer/calibration-markers-and-image-warping), [Colour spaces and colour segmentation](/egb339/temaer/colour-spaces-and-colour-segmentation), [Shape descriptors from area and perimeter](/egb339/temaer/shape-descriptors-from-area-and-perimeter) and [Inverse kinematics](/egb339/temaer/inverse-kinematics) explain the component algorithms.
- [Assessment 2 – Applied project overview](/egb339/vurderinger/assessment-2-applied-project-overview) puts both vision components in context.

## Open questions

- Which image thresholds remain stable across *all* warped examples?
- What margin above $z=31$ mm prevents a carried shape from hitting other objects?
- How can algorithm faults be separated from random setup variations using video/logs, without spending many expensive attempts?

assessment-2-3-and-2-4-pick-and-place-im.title: Assessment 2.3 and 2.4 – Self-coding pick-and-place plan
assessment-2-3-and-2-4-pick-and-place-im.summary: Eight self-coding steps with mathematics, checkpoints, safety rules, tests and oral questions. Finish simulation before porting separately to physical hardware.
assessment-2-3-and-2-4-pick-and-place-im.body:
> [!abstract] Goal
> Write a **general vision-guided pick-and-place solution yourself**. Complete and explain 2.3 in CoppeliaSim first. Then use the same vision chain in 2.4 with the physical robot's own dimensions and safety rules. This is a working/checking plan, not finished submission code. Authoritative requirements: [Assessment 2.3 – Vision simulation and oral demonstration](/egb339/vurderinger/assessment-2-3-vision-simulation-and-oral-demonstration) and [Assessment 2.4 – Vision physical robot submission](/egb339/vurderinger/assessment-2-4-vision-physical-robot-submission).

> [!warning] Integrity and source boundaries
> Official PDFs and supplied files govern the requirements. GenAI may support preparation/development, but you must verify and acknowledge AI-generated content as QUT requires. **No GenAI during the oral demonstration**; explain the algorithm with your own understanding. Do not edit source material, submit this plan, or submit/operate the physical robot before completing offline checks. [Project overview](/egb339/vurderinger/assessment-2-applied-project-overview), [2.3 requirements](/egb339/vurderinger/assessment-2-3-vision-simulation-and-oral-demonstration), [2.4 requirements](/egb339/vurderinger/assessment-2-4-vision-physical-robot-submission).

## First: what stays the same and what changes?

| | Simulation 2.3 | Physical robot 2.4 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Input | Warped `mvt.Image`, `target_positions`, simulated robot | Warped `mvt.Image`, `target_positions`, Dobot |
| Movable objects | 5: red square, blue/green circle and square | 8 visible; move the **4** named target-dictionary keys |
| Marker XY, clockwise from large red circle | $(178,22.5)$, $(223,22.5)$, $(223,-22.5)$, $(178,-22.5)$ | $(117.7,154.8)$, $(297.7,154.8)$, $(297.7,-165.2)$, $(117.7,-165.2)$ |
| $L_0,L_1,L_2,L_3,L_4$ in mm | 138, 135, 147, 60, **80** | 138, 135, 147, 60, **70** |
| Outcome | Every object moves at least 75 mm; error ≤5 mm | Four requested objects within 20 mm |
| Motion | `move_arm` sets a target; wait for completion | `move_arm` blocks; no simulator sleep |
| Critical safety | Lift before lateral movement | Never $z<6.5$ mm; lift to at least **31 mm** before lateral movement; <3 min |

Values come from [2.3](/egb339/vurderinger/assessment-2-3-vision-simulation-and-oral-demonstration) and [2.4](/egb339/vurderinger/assessment-2-4-vision-physical-robot-submission). **Never just rename the file and assume all other values match.**

## Prerequisite topics

## Step 4 — Order markers and build the homography

- [ ] Locate the four red **circles**. Start at the largest and order the other three clockwise in the **warped image**. Explicitly remember that image $v$ increases downward.
- [ ] 2.4 marker detection must tolerate some occlusion: the task allows up to 10 % of marker area to be hidden. Do not require a perfect circle in every image. [2.4 occlusion](/egb339/vurderinger/assessment-2-4-vision-physical-robot-submission).
- [ ] Pair them in the same order with the **correct variant's** known XY points. Check a noncrossing polygon and image markers that are not nearly collinear. [Calibration](/egb339/temaer/calibration-markers-and-image-warping).
- [ ] Estimate $H_{R\leftarrow I}$ from at least four corresponding planar points. An OpenCV estimator can help, but understand that $H$ has eight degrees of freedom up to scale.
- [ ] For image point $p_I=[u,v,1]^T$, calculate $q=H_{R\leftarrow I}p_I$ and $[x,y]=[q_1/q_3,q_2/q_3]$ in mm. Check $q_3\ne0$. If you estimate the opposite direction, invert $H$ before pixel→XY. [Homographies](/egb339/temaer/planar-homographies).
- [ ] Reproject all four markers and compare against the table. Four pairs can have near-zero fitting error even with wrong labels; also check orientation, workspace and an independent plausibility measure or synthetic test.

> [!tip] Checkpoint
> Markers have the task-sheet order, outputs are millimetres and objects lie in a plausible robot workspace. A controlled forward/inverse transform recovers the pixel within your numerical tolerance.

## Step 5 — Build robot goals and check IK

- [ ] Apply the measured homography to find source XY for each requested object. Use target XY from `target_positions`; do not replace it with the template placeholder.
- [ ] Choose a justified contact $z$ and higher **safe** intermediate $z$. 2.4 constrains the *tip height*, not just the object's top.
- [ ] Reuse the week-5 IK method you understand, using the correct suction geometry. Start at $\theta_1=\operatorname{atan2}(y,x)$ and solve a planar distance/height problem; check reachability before `arccos`. [IK](/egb339/temaer/inverse-kinematics), [Workspace and branches](/egb339/temaer/robot-workspace-and-ik-solution-branches).
- [ ] Test `FK(IK(goal))\approx goal` in millimetres at many points before commanding the robot. Check joint limits and both geometric branches where relevant.

> [!tip] Checkpoint
> IK returns radians for valid goals, explicitly rejects invalid goals and has a small FK return error. Test 2.3 and 2.4 with their **respective** $L_4$; do not mix in the 2.2 keyboard convention.

## Step 6 — Execute one safe pick-and-place sequence

Write motion as a readable state chain:

```text
validate object and target
suction off → above source → descend vertically → suction on
lift vertically to safe height → travel laterally above target
descend vertically → suction off → lift vertically to safe height
```

- [ ] Test one simulator object before looping over all five. Wait for simulator movement before picking/releasing; physical `move_arm` waits itself. [2.3 motion](/egb339/vurderinger/assessment-2-3-vision-simulation-and-oral-demonstration), [2.4 motion](/egb339/vurderinger/assessment-2-4-vision-physical-robot-submission).
- [ ] Physical robot: never command $z<6.5$ mm, use about $z=8$ mm contact as a **starting recommendation**, and lift to at least $z=31$ mm before lateral movement after picking/releasing. Use more clearance, e.g. 50 mm, if IK/workspace permit. Check **every** lateral segment. Tip clearance alone does not guarantee collision-free motion of every robot link.
- [ ] Keep suction active until the object reaches its target. Release, then lift. No diagonal/lateral motion while the carried object is low.

> [!warning] The source's 30/31 mm ambiguity
> 2.4's abort list requires at least **31 mm**, while a later recommendation says 30 mm. This plan uses the stricter 31 mm limit with a safety margin. [2.4 safety](/egb339/vurderinger/assessment-2-4-vision-physical-robot-submission).

## Oral practice for 2.3

1. **Why four calibration markers?** A planar $3\times3$ homography has eight independent parameters up to scale; every correspondence gives two equations. Four noncollinear pairs are the minimum. [Homography](/egb339/temaer/planar-homographies).
2. **Why order them?** H is estimated from *pairs*, not unordered sets. Wrong pairing can reflect/twist the result despite small fitting error. [Calibration](/egb339/temaer/calibration-markers-and-image-warping).
3. **What does the last component of $Hp$ mean?** Divide homogeneous coordinates by the third component to obtain ordinary XY. Zero does not represent a finite Euclidean point. [Homography](/egb339/temaer/planar-homographies).
4. **How distinguish circle and square?** Threshold → blob → area/perimeter → circularity; ideal values 1 and $\pi/4$ guide you, but noise/pixel boundaries require tolerance. [Shape](/egb339/temaer/shape-descriptors-from-area-and-perimeter).
5. **Why median for salt-and-pepper noise?** It replaces an isolated extreme by a neighbourhood median; an oversized window can remove small markers. [Filtering](/egb339/temaer/spatial-filtering-and-convolution).
6. **What fails under changed illumination?** Absolute RGB thresholds shift. Ratios/HSV help common intensity scaling, not all colour casts, saturation or reflections. [Chromaticity](/egb339/temaer/colour-normalization-and-chromaticity).
7. **Why not one homography for all 3D?** It applies to one plane; height offsets, lens distortion and calibration faults cause coordinate error. [Week 11](/egb339/uker/uke-11).
8. **Vision or robot fault?** Inspect intermediate masks, labels/centroids, marker pairs, reprojection, FK error and actual final positions separately. [2.3](/egb339/vurderinger/assessment-2-3-vision-simulation-and-oral-demonstration).
